items.stem: Why is checking only the HTTP status code insufficient when testing an API response?

options.text: A correct status can still accompany a wrong or malformed response body
options.rationale: Correct: status and payload are independent; both must be validated.

options.text: Status codes are always 200 regardless of outcome
options.rationale: Status codes vary and carry real meaning.

options.text: The body is never part of an API response
options.rationale: Most responses include a body that must be checked.

options.text: Schema validation replaces the need for any assertions
options.rationale: Schema validation complements, not replaces, other assertions.

items.explanation: Correct: status and payload are independent; both must be validated.
items.domain_ref: Status codes, schemas and response validation

items.stem: Which responses should an authorization test assert? (Select TWO)

options.text: 401 Unauthorized when no valid credentials are supplied
options.rationale: Correct: 401 signals missing or invalid authentication.

options.text: 403 Forbidden when the caller is authenticated but lacks the required scope
200 OK for every request regardless of credentials
options.rationale: Returning 200 for unauthorised calls is a security defect.

options.text: 500 Internal Server Error for a missing token
options.rationale: A missing token should yield 401, not a server error.

items.explanation: Correct: 401 signals missing or invalid authentication.; Correct: 403 signals authenticated-but-not-permitted.

items.stem: What does a consumer-driven contract test verify?

options.text: That the provider meets the expectations the consumer actually depends on
options.rationale: Correct: the consumer's needs define the contract the provider must satisfy.

options.text: That the entire system passes an end-to-end scenario
options.rationale: That is end-to-end testing, broader than a contract test.

options.text: That the database schema is normalised
options.rationale: Contract tests are about API expectations, not DB normalisation.
UI rendering is outside an API contract test.

items.explanation: Correct: the consumer's needs define the contract the provider must satisfy.
